newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Generali, Austrian concern, said to eye Postabank.
newsitem.headline: Generali, Austrian concern, said to eye Postabank.

text.p: E.A. Generali Group may be interested in increasing its stake in Hungary's Postabank but would have to see details first, a spokesman for E.A. Generali said on Friday.
The spokesman, Josef Hlinka, also said there is "at least one bigger Austrian investor with interest in investing in Postabank", but he declined to say who it was.

"You know that possibly the Postabank will increase its capital...and when Postabank will do it maybe they will ask us to participate but so far there is no offer for such an increase in their capital," Hlinka said.
"We will see what's going on when they make such an offer...It depends on the conditions and we do not know the conditions right now. But when there will be an offer...we will see what we can do."
E.A. Generali holds about a five percent stake in Postabank, Hungary's second biggest commercial bank.
Robert Muranyi, deputy chief executive officer of Postabank, said many investors were interested but he declined to identify them.
He said the expressions of interest had come from "inside and outside Europe" and that investment bank SBC Warburg was handling the negotiations.
The bank, which was hit by a panic withdrawal of deposits of about 24 billion forints at the end of February, last month reported after-tax profit for 1996 of 5.6 million forints.
The figure was sharply reduced compared with a pre-tax profit figure of 3.165 billion forints published by the bank in a preliminary report on February 14.
